AC.purpose: The purpose of this Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) is to establish procedures that ensure access controls adhere to VA directives, VA Knowledge Service policies, and National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) standards and guidelines. This SOP is intended for those responsible for managing, using, accessing, or operating the VA PARS information system.
AC.scope: This SOP is applicable to all staff involved in the implementation and management of access controls to include the account management lifecycle.

roles.name: Information System Owner (ISO)
responsibilities: Ensure adherence to access control policies by key Office of Information and Technology (OIT) staff.
Oversee personnel with significant responsibility for information systems.
Update procedures as needed to ensure they meet OIT mission requirements and comply with federal laws, policies, procedures, and guidelines.
Ensure all procedures herein are properly followed.

roles.name: Information Systems Security Officer (ISSO)
responsibilities: Monitor and audit access controls to ensure adherence to VA Knowledge Service.

roles.name: Account Managers/OIT Support Staff
responsibilities: Manage the entire lifecycle of accounts (e.g., create, enable, modify, disable, and remove) for the information systems to ensure compliance with account management.
Promptly take appropriate actions on accounts as requested.

roles.name: Contracting Officer Representative (COR)
responsibilities: Designate individuals to act as a liaison between OIT Account Managers and the service to authorize and submit access requests.
Ensure all access requests comply with background investigation completion, training, and Rules of Behavior (ROB) completion prior to request.
Promptly report changes on a user’s employment status or change of duties to OIT staff to ensure all accounts are acted on appropriately.

roles.name: Product Owner
responsibilities: Monitor and audit access controls to ensure adherence to VA Knowledge Service.
Perform monthly New User Access Request reviews.
Perform quarterly Privileged Account reviews.
Perform quarterly Separated User reviews.
Perform Inactive Account reviews every 90 calendar days.
Function as the designated individual for respective service to submit access requests.
Promptly report changes on a user’s employment status or change of duties to OIT staff to ensure all accounts are acted on appropriately.
Ensures all access requests comply with background investigation completion, training, and ROB completion prior to request submission.

AT.purpose: » This SOP establishes procedures for the implementation of Awareness and Training Security controls at VA PARS in accordance with Federal Law, VA policy, and the Office of Information Security (OIS) requirements.
AT.scope: » This SOP outlines procedures that apply to Information System Owners, ISSO, Product Owner, Talent Management System (TMS) Administrators, and Developers.
AT.policy: Initial and annual information security awareness training is mandatory for all individuals who have been granted access to VA-owned information system resources. Supervisors and CORs will ensure that employees and contractors within their area of responsibility (AOR) complete all applicable security role-based training (RBT) within 30 days of occupying a position with security RBT requirements. All VA PARS team members will follow the procedures outlined in this document.

roles.name: Information System Owner and Product Owner
responsibilities: Ensure the SOPs set forth in this document are followed by the individuals under their responsibility.

roles.name: ISSO
responsibilities: Provide security awareness training at new employee orientation (NEO).
Monitor compliance with the security awareness and training requirements for each system user.
Coordinate, monitor, and conduct periodic reviews to ensure compliance with the VA National or Contractor ROB requirement for users of VA information systems and VA information.

Serve as the primary point of contact (POC) for security awareness and training within their AOR for this requirement for VA staff and partners who work remotely or are considered tenants of their closest VA facility resides with the employee/partner’s parent organization.

Notify the IT Operations and Services (ITOPS) when users are non-compliant with security training requirements so their computer accounts can be disabled in accordance with VA policy. » Notify TMS domain administrator(s) when training cannot be verified by the ISSO by comparing the AD report to the TMS daily reports.
Complete quarterly audits to ensure that users with special privileges and/or roles have the appropriate security RBT.

roles.name: Product Owner
responsibilities: Assure all VA PARS development team members are enrolled in TMS and their TMS accounts remain properly configured to facilitate accurate reporting. This includes, but is not limited to, ensuring all user TMS accounts are: Active Assigned to the correct TMS domain Using the assigned “va.gov” government employee email address
Work with services and users to update and correct any TMS account deficiencies as needed.
Immediately merge duplicated accounts into a single TMS account for the user.

roles.name: Managers and supervisors will:
responsibilities: Assure all users within their AOR remain in compliance with all information security and RBT, as appropriate.
Ensure that the TMS records of their employees are assigned to the correct supervisor.

roles.name: All VA PARS users with access to VA-owned information system resources will:
responsibilities: Complete Privacy and Information Security Awareness Training prior to receiving access to VA-owned information system resources, and at least annually thereafter. In addition, the VA Privacy and Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) training, as well as any applicable security RBT, will be completed as required by VA Knowledge Service.
Log into their TMS account every 30 calendar days at a minimum to ensure that the account remains active.

Use the assigned va.gov government employee email address as the primary contact email and assure the correct address is listed. If the TMS account is inactive, or the user’s supervisor name is incorrect, the TMS domain administrator will be alerted.

roles.name: Human Resources
responsibilities: Correct any errors in the HR Smart database that are causing errors in the TMS database.

roles.name: Initial Security Awareness Training:
responsibilities: NEO: This training helps employees, contractors, and other users of VA computer systems understand their responsibility to protect sensitive information and information systems.
Prior to being granted system access, all users will either attend the ISSO-led training during NEO or complete VA Privacy and Information Security Awareness Training with ROB in TMS.
Users who have completed FISMA-compliant training within the previous 365 days, either with VA or another Federal Agency, are the only exception to this requirement.

Employees of other Federal agencies are required to sign the VA ROB prior to being provided access to VA’s information systems or VA sensitive information. AU.purpose: This SOP has been created to support and facilitate the implementation of the Auditing and Accountability Policy and Applicable security controls. The procedures outlined in this document are consistent with VA Directives and VA Policies, VA OIT Knowledge Services, and the VA Handbook 6500.2. The purpose of this SOP is to support and supplement VA PARS auditing capabilities and processes. This document is intended to complement existing VA Directives and Policies.
AU.scope: This SOP is applicable to all VA PARS staff involved in development, execution, and reporting procedures for incident response.
AU.policy: » Audit trails can assist in detecting security violations, system performance problems, and application flaws. Audit trails may also help in identifying problems that are not related to security incidents or intrusions. » VA PARS is responsible for regularly reviewing and analyzing audit records for indications of inappropriate or unusual activity and investigating suspicious activity. Any security-related incidents will be immediately reported to the appropriate ISSO and to the VA Cyber Security Operations Center (CSOC). Logs should be maintained for a minimum of one year and should be reviewed/monitored by the Product Owner, or designee, daily. The appropriate ISSO will audit this process to ensure the reviewed events are corrected. » All staff with audit roles and responsibilities will comply with the procedures outlined within this SOP. » VA PARS Product Owner will establish and review adequate audit trails to assist in detecting security violations, system performance problems, and application flaws. In addition, additional audit trails should be established to identify problems that are not related to security violations or intrusions such as fluctuations of system resources. » All audit records will be properly documented and maintained as required by National Archive Records Administration (NARA) retention periods and/or HIPAA legislation. » To ensure VA PARS meets the retainability period, periodic backups will be determined and conducted. All system backup audit records will be logically separated from the system or system component that is being audited.

roles.name: ISO or Designee
responsibilities: Monitor and investigate security violations for activities involving access and modification of files within the information systems.
Determine and enable audit logs at the application level and document what audit events will be monitored for VA PARS.
Determine and implement audit log events.
Determine privilege users with authorized access to management of audit functionality at the application level.

roles.name: ISSO
responsibilities: Coordinate all audit logs to identify security violations and/or incidents.
Ensure the System Owner and IT personnel implement audit procedures in accordance with VA guidelines and policies.
Coordinate with ISO, Product Owner, CSOC, and Privacy Officer (PO) to ensure corrective steps are taken to minimize and resolve security events.

roles.name: ITOPS/Enterprise Cloud Solutions Office (ECSO)
responsibilities: Monitors information system audit logs and ensure corrective steps are taken to minimize and resolve security events.
Report any suspicious security event to the ISO and ISSO.

roles.name: Privacy Officer
responsibilities: Review and monitor all audit logs to identify privacy violations and/or incidents.

CA.purpose: This SOP establishes procedures for the implementation of Security Assessment and Authorization (CA) security controls at VA PARS in accordance with federal law, VA policy, and OIS requirements.
CA.scope: This SOP outlines procedures that apply to those involved in the implementation of the CA security controls for the VA PARS. This includes the ISO, ISSO, System Steward(s), PO, and all information system users.
CA.policy: The system-specific procedures outlined in this SOP are intended to ensure compliance with: » VA Directive 6500 » VA Knowledge Service » VA Handbook 6500.3 » NIST Special Publication 800-53, Revision 4 » NIST Special Publication 800-37

roles.name: ISO
responsibilities: Ensure that the information system complies with the NIST Special Publication 800-53.
Assigns a System Steward to facilitate implementation of the system’s CA security controls.
Cooperate with independent assessors or assessment teams when they conduct security control assessments of VA PARS.
Submit the system for (re)authorization no less than 70 days prior to the expiration of its current Authorization to Operate (ATO), or when the system undergoes significant changes.

When an interconnection is to be established, initiate, and complete the Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) or Interconnection Security Agreement (ISA) intake form: Work with the ISSO to evaluate security requirements for proposed and ongoing interconnections. Work with third-party companies to set up network interconnections.
Verify that devices are authorized to be connected to the VA network via the information system.

roles.name: Information System Security Officer (ISSO)
responsibilities: Monitor the security controls in the information system on an ongoing basis for effectiveness and adequacy of system security controls using the VA Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) tool.
Cooperate with independent assessors or assessment teams when they conduct security control assessments of VA PARS.

Ensure that interconnections are properly authorized and documented using MOU/ISAs by: Verifying the security content in the MOU/ISA is accurate and reporting deficiencies to the document stakeholders. Uploading draft and final MOU/ISA documents to the MOU/ISA document site portal Confirming that completed MOU/ISAs are uploaded to applicable security controls in the GRC tool. Aiding and guiding stakeholders through the system interconnection approval process Providing cybersecurity subject matter expertise for MOU/ISA content • Reviewing local MOU/ISAs annually to ensure security controls are still in place.

Maintain records/documents to show that the information system: Undergoes assessment of designated security controls in the information system Analyzes for impact to documents and reports changes to, or deficiencies in, the operation of the security controls. Documents weaknesses in a Plan of Action & Milestones (POA&M) using the designated VA-approved GRC tool.

roles.name: System Steward(s)
responsibilities: Document and test security controls
Work with the ISO and ISSO to make updates to the system security documentation in the VA GRC tool.

roles.name: Privacy Officer (PO)
responsibilities: Ensure that interconnections are properly authorized and documented using MOU/ISAs Manage the risks and business impacts of privacy laws and policies. Assist the cybersecurity team with ensuring privacy requirements are included for all interconnections.

roles.name: Other information system stakeholders’ personnel
responsibilities: Ensure that system security controls are accurately assessed by working with other system stakeholders to assess and provide information that facilitates the assessment of the system’s security controls.

CM.purpose: The purpose of this SOP is to establish the configuration management procedures required by the configuration management security control for the VA PARS computer system(s) as outlined in VA Directive 6500. The intent of this document is to facilitate the implementation of VA PARS procedures for NIST controls. All assigned employees are required to comply with this SOP as required by VA Directive 6500. OIT reviews and updates the current configuration management policies and applicable procedures every 5 years. VA Directive 6500 contains the System Configuration Management Policy for VA OIT. VA OIT outlined VA’s system security controls based on the current version of NIST SP 800-53 and Committee on National Security Systems (CNSS) Instruction No. 1253, which are required for the effective implementation of the configuration management family. The controls and procedures in this document are consistent with applicable laws: executive orders, policies, regulations, standards, and guidance. They will be periodically reviewed and, when necessary, updated.
CM.scope: This SOP governs information system configuration management activities. The procedures outlined in this SOP apply to all VA PARS personnel responsible for implementing this control family.
CM.policy: VA PARS team will implement the configuration management SOP section of the POM to facilitate the implementation of the configuration management policy and associated configuration management controls. The ISO or designee will develop and disseminate procedures to facilitate the implementation of the configuration management policy and associated controls. These procedures include purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance. VA PARS staff will collaborate, participate, and recognize the shared, related, and interdependent responsibility to provide effective and efficient information security to the information system. VA PARS team will follow the procedures outlined in this document. The designated authority will review annually, and update as needed, the configuration management procedures. VA PARS adheres to system development (SD) configuration management requirements at the enterprise level along with those of the VA PARS SOP to facilitate the implementation of the configuration management policy and associated controls. This SOP is developed to facilitate the implementation and management of CM controls at the information system level. The VA PARS SOP is disseminated to all personnel responsible for configuration management responsibilities.

roles.name: ISO
responsibilities: Fulfill the role of ISO within the GRC tool and is referred to as ISO within this SOP.
Ensure the procedures set forth in this document are followed by the individuals under their responsibility.

Review the SOP annually and update as necessary. Notify VA PARS staff of all changes and updates to this SOP using the OIT CRR ACOE Technical Solutions All Staff (alias: TSAll@va.gov) Distribution Group (DG).
Is responsible for fulfilling their role as ISO within the GRC tool.
Is responsible for maintaining a complete and accurate inventory of IT assets to include: Software and licensing Web applications Databases

Develop a configuration management plan (CMP) for the information system that establishes a process for managing the configuration of the configuration items. The plan establishes a process for identifying configuration items throughout the SD lifecycle.
Play integral role in the assessment and security impact analysis of local new or proposed information systems.
Monitor and respond to unauthorized changes and security incidents.
Approve and review privileged user access to the information system as well as the logical access to information systems.

Ensure that all: VA PARS personnel adhere to VA policies, procedures, bulletins, and memorandums relative to NIST Special Publication 800-53 Security Controls and Assessment Procedures for Federal Information Systems and Organizations. Product Owner schedules, records, and documents all changes to an information system or application in accordance with VA Directive 6004, Configuration, Change, and Release Management Programs. Technical Advisor follows VA Enterprise baseline configuration standards and change management procedures.

roles.name: Technical Advisor
responsibilities: Under the direction and assignment of the ISO, the Technical Advisor maintains inventory of information system components within their boundary.
Responsible for maintaining: • Routine validations of assets
Manages conformance with VA OIT security policies by decommissioning information systems and completing appropriate records.
Update the inventory of information system components as an integral part of information system updates.

roles.name: System Steward
responsibilities: Responsible for fulfilling their role as system steward within the GRC tool.

Responsibilities include: Assigning user roles to generate an RMF security authorization package. Maintaining system-level information Managing the System’s security categorization Creating POA&M items Documenting control correlation identifier (CCI) compliance and control implementation status Uploading and managing artifacts Initiating workflows and package submission

roles.name: Information Systems Security Officer (ISSO)
responsibilities: Confirm that configuration management and change control procedures are documented for each system in the RMF GRC tool.
Play an integral role in the assessment and security impact analysis of new and proposed information systems.
Fulfill their role as ISSO within the GRC tool.

CP.purpose: The purpose of this SOP is to establish procedures for VA PARS by providing mandatory processes for contingency planning operations.
CP.scope: The intent of this document is to detail the procedures for VA PARS implementation of contingency planning controls as defined by NIST. Contingency planning controls are intended to facilitate the continuation of critical services and business practices and allow the organization to return to its daily operations as quickly as possible after an unforeseen event. They also help protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information systems during interruption and restoration of information systems.
CP.policy: VA PARS team is required to comply with this Contingency Planning SOP as required by Knowledge Services. This SOP requires staff to collaborate, participate, and recognize the shared, related, and interdependent responsibilities to provide effective and efficient security to information system(s).

roles.name: ISO and/or Designee
responsibilities: Distribute the Information System Contingency Plan (ISCP) documents to authorized recipients.
Conduct contingency plan testing for the application at least annually and after any major change to ISCP procedures.
Activate contingency operations as needed.
Communicate with VAEC personnel as needed to facilitate recovery and reconstitution procedures.

roles.name: ISSO
responsibilities: Advise VA PARS team in the contingency planning process.
Coordinate with VA PARS and VAEC to assure contingency planning and testing is conducted at least annually.
Work with ISO and/or designee to gather test results from services to determine if ISCP procedures are adequate.
Work with contingency planning officials to implement lessons learned as needed.

roles.name: VA PARS Development Team
responsibilities: Support contingency operations/procedures under the direction of the ISO and/or designee.

IA.purpose: The purpose of this SOP is to facilitate the implementation of NIST 800-53, Revision 4 Identification and Authentication (IA) controls, VA Handbook 6500, RMF for VA Information Systems – Tier 3: VA Information Security Program, VA Handbook 6500.2.
IA.scope: This SOP is applicable to all VA PARS team involved in the development, execution, and reporting procedures for the NIST IA control family. The information contained in this IA SOP is intended to maintain the operating system of VA PARS addressing and managing identification and authentication of users and assets within the VA PARS application. It will also help protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of VA PARS for continuance of essential missions and business functions. It also helps limit damage and reduce recovery time and costs. All VA PARS team members are required to comply with this IA SOP per the VA Handbook 6500.
IA.policy: A robust IA policy decreases the risk of unauthorized access to information systems. The VA PARS team will collaborate, participate, and recognize the shared, related, and interdependent responsibility to provide effective and efficient information security to the VA PARS application. All VA PARS team members and contractors will follow the procedures outlined in this document.

roles.name: ISO and/or Designee
responsibilities: ISO is ultimately responsible for the full management and operation of VA PARS.

ISO may delegate the following responsibilities noted below: Ensuring that the SOP set forth in this document are followed by the individuals under his/her responsibility. Ensuring that security violations involving IA occurring within their assigned area of management control are reported to the appropriate ISSO. Ensuring that all employees, contractors, and other individuals within their assigned area of management control who develop, operate, administer, maintain, or use VA PARS understand they are responsible for reporting actual or suspected security incidents to their immediate supervisor or ISSO.

roles.name: ISSO
responsibilities: Ensure that the IA control is being satisfied by the security measures that were implemented.
Work with OIT technical staff to determine the nature and scope of security incidents.
Track, report, and close out security violations and incidents in PSETS.

IR.purpose: » To facilitate the implementation of the NIST SP 800-53 Security and Privacy Controls for Federal Information Systems and Organizations, NIST 800-61 Computer Security Incident Handling Guide, RMF for VA Information Systems – Tier 3: VA Information Security Program, VA Handbook 6500.2 Management of Breaches Involving Sensitive Personal Information, and ESO Incident Response Reporting, Training, and Testing SOP. » VA PARS system security controls are based on the current version of NIST SP 800-53 and the Committee on National Security Systems (CNSS) Instruction No. 1253, which are required for the effective implementation of the Incident Response family.
IR.scope: This SOP applies to VA PARS ISSO, Privacy Officer, ISO, Product Owner, and VA PARS team members.

roles.name: ISO and/or designee
responsibilities: Incident Preparation: Maintain current VA PARS incident response contact information. Make training available as appropriate and necessary to the VA PARS incident response personnel. Ensure that all users of VA information and information systems under their responsibility take annual privacy training. Work closely with the ISSO to maintain continuity of service. Ensure that all users of VA information and information systems under their responsibility take ownership/responsibility for the data at their disposal.

Incident Prevention: Adhere to VA configuration standards to ensure application setups are appropriately configurated and maintained. Ensure the appropriate user awareness and training programs on privacy procedures are available. Ensure that users are aware of the reporting procedures and the policies in place to protect information systems, employees, and property. Maintain a strong working relationship with the ISSO and Privacy Officer. Ensure systems and subsystems affected by incidents are isolated as quickly as possible and, if necessary, are restored and/or rebuilt.

Incident Detection: Implement enterprise tools in a timely fashion. Provide consistent monitoring and automated alert implementation. Maintain a strong working relationship with staff to encourage reporting of incidents/suspected incidents.
Incident Analysis Maintain pertinent information including audit and event logs as well as user account information when appropriate.

Incident Documentation: Provide updates to open incidents as directed. Provide input as required in any documentation requested from top management both inside and outside the VA PARS. Safeguard data and sensitive information related to the incident. Ensure that access to incident data is properly restricted.

Containment Strategy Coordinate and advise in the execution of the containment strategy and efforts at the application level. Make decisions about containment actions. Coordinate response actions until incidents are resolved. Report to senior VA officials on the status of incidents. Work with the OIT and VAEC staff to assure containment actions are performed in a timely and efficient manner. Safeguard the integrity of involved software as appropriate.
Evidence Gathering and Management Preserve software as appropriate and requested. Preserve audit and event logs as appropriate.

Corrective/Mitigation Action Balance mission needs with recommended risk mitigation. Own the restoration plan. Coordinate with Network ISSOs, Privacy Officers, and staff to implement eradication and remediation actions. Implement recommendations as appropriate. Maintain a record of costs associated with repair, restoration, business disruption, and labor.

Lessons Learned Participate with the VA PARS incident response staff in an incident postmortem review of all documentation surrounding the incident/suspected incident. Implement “best practices” as appropriate based on the review.

roles.name: Appropriate Information System Security Officer (ISSO)
responsibilities: Incident Preparation Obtain and maintain PSETS user account. Be aware of the security laws, regulations, and policies that apply to the organization. Review incident response policy and procedures annually. Communicate to individuals within the organization to report suspected incidents as soon as identified or discovered to the ISSO(s). Ensure the Incident Response Plan (IRP) test is conducted annually.

Incident Prevention Advise users on proper security protocols to prevent incidents. Ensure training compliance within 30 days of assuming an IR role or responsibility and annually thereafter. Follow AT Awareness and Training SOP.

Incident Detection Communicate protective measures received from VA-Cyber Security Operations Center (VACSOC) when an incident or vulnerability is discovered. Ensure that incidents are properly reported, responses are coordinated, and incident updates are provided as required. Coordinate with the PO to determine if a detected or reported security incident is also a privacy incident.

Incident Analysis Enter all reported incidents into the PSETS within one (1) hour of receiving or identifying an incident. Complete a risk evaluation within PSETS using the “Information at Risk” tab at the time of reporting the incident and update PSETS information accordingly.

Incident Documentation For events, not in a “closed” status, review on a regular basis, and document updates within PSETS when new or relevant information has been obtained. Track the progress of response activity via a PSETS event if the event is determined to be a breach and perform all necessary documentation of progress. Ensure redacted copies of pertinent external communications (i.e., email, letters, web page, etc.) have been attached to the PSETS event. PSET tickets were remediated when remediation instructions were received from VA- CSOC.

Incident Notification Notify VA PARS team and support staff of the incident. Keep VA PARS team and support staff apprised of any changes or updates regarding the incident. Containment Strategy Participate in initiating containment actions and suggest alternate containment actions, as necessary.

Evidence Gathering and Management Execute direction provided by the Data Breach Response Service, VA-CSOC, law enforcement, or the Office of the Inspector General (OIG). Consult with law enforcement or the OIG as necessary. Log all comments and details of their investigation into PSETS ticket.
Lessons Learned Incorporate lessons learned during ongoing incident handling activities into the specific IR handling procedures in the VA PARS IRP and VA PARS IR SOP.

roles.name: Privacy Officer (PO)
responsibilities: Incident Preparation Take appropriate privacy and security training. Obtain and maintain a PSETS account and develop familiarity with the system. Review VA Handbook 6502.1, Privacy Event Tracking. Review PSETS Basic User’s Handbook. Maintain awareness of the privacy laws, regulations, and policies that affect their organizations. Ensure that individuals within their organizations know who their POs are. Acquire template of Incident Notification/Credit Monitoring letter. Establish a working relationship with the ISSO(s) for their organizations. Ensure that VA PARS team members have appropriate incident response mechanisms, such as phone numbers, email addresses, and tools available to report suspected privacy incidents to the PO. Ensure an After-Action Report (AAR) process for privacy incidents is in place to look at root causes and future prevention mechanisms.

Incident Prevention Implement Departmental and appropriate Administration privacy policies and procedures. Establish an internal privacy audit or compliance monitoring and audit program. Report that individuals in their organizations complete the appropriate annual Privacy training(s). Ensure that privacy issues and concerns are communicated to and coordinated with appropriate parties. Participate in the review of Privacy Threshold Assessments (PTA) and Privacy Impact Assessments (PIA) for systems within the purview of their organizations. Understand what constitutes a Privacy Act System of Records (SOR) and ensure that all PII that is retrieved by individuals’ names or other unique identifiers are maintained in an official SOR published in the Federal Register. Promote activities to foster privacy awareness (e.g., Privacy Day or Information Protection Awareness Week).

Incident Detection Receive complaints from Veterans or anyone within their organization who believes an incident has occurred. Enter all complaints received into the system allotted e.g., PSETS, the reporting of incidents within one (1) hour of discovery. Follow guidance provided by the VA Privacy Service to record all incidents in PSETS. Monitor all incidents and complaints entered in PSETS. Provide updates to PSETS, as appropriate.

Incident Documentation For events not in a “closed” status, review on a regular basis, and document updates within PSETS when new or relevant information has been obtained. Track the progress of response activity via a PSETS event, if the event is determined to be a breach, and perform all necessary documentation of progress. Ensure redacted copies of pertinent external communications (i.e., email, letters, web page, etc.) have been attached to the PSETS event. Ensure redacted copies of notification and/or credit protection letters are attached to PSETS events as required.

Incident Notification Notify VA PARS team members and support staff of the incident. Keep VA PARS team members and support staff apprised of any changes or updates regarding the incident. Prepare Incident Notification/Credit Monitoring Letters for signature. Obtain Promo Codes for credit monitoring letters when applicable.
Containment Strategy Participate in initiating containment actions when there is a privacy component. Suggest containment actions, as necessary.
Restoration Ensure timely closure of incidents and complaints.

Evidence Gathering and Management Execute direction provided by the Data Breach Response Service, VA-CSOC, law enforcement, and the OIG. Begin fact-finding investigation and log all comments and details of the investigation into PSETS or the subsequent system designated for the reporting of privacy complaints and incidents once the initial complaint or incident is logged into PSETS. Consult with law enforcement, OIG, or other investigatory agencies as necessary.
Lessons Learned Log resolution of incident or complaint

PS.purpose: This SOP has been created to support and facilitate Personnel Security (PS) controls at VA PARS. The procedures outlined in this document are consistent with VA Directives and VA Policies, VA Knowledge Service, and VA Handbook 6500.2. The purpose of this SOP is to establish procedures for providing mandatory safeguard processes for the PS controls for VA PARS team members involved with the management, operation, and personnel security of the VA PARS information system.
PS.scope: This SOP is applicable to VA PARS COR who is involved in the onboarding and offboarding process for VA PARS team members.
PS.policy: The intent of this document is to facilitate the implementation of PS controls as outlined by the NIST. VA PARS is required to follow published VA policies and regulations which establish criteria and procedures for making suitability determinations and taking suitability actions involving applicants for and appointees to covered positions. Suitability determinations are based on a person’s character or conduct that may have an impact on the integrity or efficiency of the service. Determining suitability for Federal employment will be consistent with 5 Part Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) 731. Determining fitness for contractor employees will be based on criteria equivalent to that used for Federal employees. Determinations made under this category are distinct from determinations of eligibility for assignment to, or retention in, sensitive national security positions. All VA PARS team members are required to comply with this PS SOP. This SOP requires VA PARS team members to collaborate, participate, and recognize the shared, related, and interdependent responsibility to provide effective and efficient personnel security services.

roles.name: Human Resources (HR) Management Offices will:
responsibilities: Ensure all positions are designated with the appropriate risk or sensitivity level in accordance with the Position Designation Application Tool (PDAT) and ensure that each appointee and employee receive a background investigation commensurate with the position risk or sensitivity level.

Ensure position risk and sensitivity level designations are consistently applied to all positions in accordance with 5 CFR Part 731, Suitability, and 5 CFR Part 732, National Security Positions, and the VA Knowledge Service. When appropriate, refer appointees and employees in Public Trust and National Security positions to the Security and Investigations Center (SIC) for initiation and adjudication of the investigation.

Ensure appointees and employees in Low Risk/non-sensitive positions have background investigations initiated and adjudicated at the local level within established timeframes. Adjudicative determinations must be made by appropriately trained personnel and reported to the Office of Personnel Management (OPM).

Ensure a fingerprint Special Agreement Check (SAC) is conducted on all new appointees who are exempt from the requirement to have a National Agency Check with Inquiries (NACI) or higher-level investigation. Whenever possible, the SAC should be performed prior to the appointee’s entrance on duty. When this is not possible, the SAC must be performed as part of the in-processing procedures. Ensure the SAC is adjudicated by appropriately trained personnel no later than 5 workdays after the results are received.
Ensure all VA PARS team members and contractors are successfully in-processed to and out- processed from the organization.

The SOW (or other defining documentation related to the contract) must be reviewed using the PDAT and given the appropriate designation.
Ensure all contractor employees who are not exempt from the investigative requirement are referred to the SIC for initiation and adjudication of the appropriate level of investigation.

Ensure a SAC is initiated on all new contractor employees who are exempt from investigative requirements and who provide direct and/or ancillary health care services at VA facilities or have access to VA information systems or sensitive information per VA Directive 0710 May 2, 2016.
Ensure the SAC is adjudicated by appropriately trained personnel no later than 5 business days after the results are received.
Ensure appropriate personnel security contract clauses are included in the contracts.

VA security policies protect and control VA-sensitive information throughout the acquisition life cycle.
SA.scope: This SOP is applicable to VA PARS COR who is involved in the generation of requirements and the procurement of, IT products and acquisition of external information system requirements for ensuring that contract documents contain adequate security requirements. The information in this SOP is intended to maintain the operational environment of the information systems and allows the organization to monitor any environmental activity. It will also help protect the CIA information systems for continuance of essential mission and business functions that limit damage and reduce recovery time and costs.
SA.policy: The intent of this document is to facilitate the VA PARS implementation procedures for NIST SP 800-53 SA security controls. VA PARS team members are to comply with the SA SOP as required by VA Directive 6500, VA Handbook 6500.6, and VA Handbook 6500.5. This SOP requires ISO and staff offices to collaborate, participate, and recognize the shared, related, and interdependent responsibility to provide effective and efficient information security to the information system. All VA PARS team members will follow the procedures outlined in this document. System and Service Acquisition (SA) is part of the SDLC and encompasses NIST SP 800-12, Introduction to Computer Security and NIST SP 800-37, Guide for Applying the Risk Management Framework to Federal Information Systems. The SA SOP requires that information security requirements be managed throughout the phases of the SDLC. Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Circular A-130 defines capital planning and investment control as a management process for ongoing identification, selection, control, and evaluation of investments in information resources. The VA determines the resources (funding, staffing, etc.) required for the cybersecurity requirements to protect the information system or information system service as part of its Planning, Programming, and Budget Execution process (PPBE).
